questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was both motivated by personal connections but also by the vast career opportunities that are in Brussels as a political science student

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information meeting in the stat of the semester helped a lot, however, it lacked social activities.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Purely informational as there were 1-2 days og information introduction by the coordinators.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I wish it took a more social nature so that you could get to know your peers.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty normal, but I would advise to start early. There are websites both for co-habitations and for apartments. I used immoweb for apartments.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try and find a good studio/co-housing close to uni - in lxelles, etterbeek or saint-gilles

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not have student accom. but there is a lot of sharing houses

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When you arrivie you have 2 additional weeks to choose your final courses. In that time you may take any course you'd like to try out, which is great. After that you have to fill in a form with your final choices.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: both email with 1-2 day responds time from coordinators and also physical meetings were possible

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to register for all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Explore the different courses when you get there and then make your decision.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels of the course strongly depend on the professor, therefore it is a good idea to attend in the fisrt weeks to get a feeling about their strictness. Generally, I found the level of master courses alright, and some were very easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is more important to make sure to attend as many classes as possible as you may be tested in the contents of class discussions, however, the exams are fairly easy - presentations, multiple choice, open questions, oral exams. But it is good to know that most exams are written in hand.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Globalization Studies
Migration and Gender
Gender and Social Movements
Terrorism and International Law
International Environmental Politics
Democratisation and Autocratisation
additional: French course

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Migration anf Gender, Gender and Social Movements both had fairly easy exams while also presenting interesting content and active participation as part of the grade.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: As I was in brussels for a year i registered at the commune and an ID costs around 50 euro

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is less expensive than copenhagen - I recommend shopping in Lidl or Colruyt

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not participate but there is a pretty broad sports club at the uni

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Broad sports club, hanging out at campus in cafees

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of cultural and fun things happening all the time in Brussels, look at facebook/instagram pages and visitbrussels. there are a lot of flee markets as well in the spring/early fall.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you drink there is a lot of beers and bars, the best fries, traveling around the country is also nice; Brugge, Ghent, Antwerpen, Knokke

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I already knew people in Brussels so fairly easy, but also if you do not know anyone, most people are super open and there are  lot of international people looking for community in the city. It is a more caotic city than Copenhagen so be ready for that

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: A lot of them mainly speak french so if you could learn a little it would be good. Otherwise just try to approach people in your class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
I dont mind it too much, but it is def. a more 'southern' mentality of seeing where things go and going with the flow than in
Denmark.It
is also more chaotic and administrative things may take some time, however, at uni the admin is pretty fast.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: More social culture of going out and doing different things also great food from all over the world

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy it!! there are a lot of amazing people and other exchange students to hang out with
2. Attend class more - but there is less reading
2. Make sure you really explore the city

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, just that the coordinators are super fast and helpful so do not be scared to reach out to them. Also it is important to address your teachers as professor and/or madame/monsieur [last name]

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting my amazing erasmus friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: getting registered in brussels - but you won't have to do that for one semester;)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
